world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Foley, William A. 2006. Universal constraints and local conditions in pidginization: case studies from New Guinea. JPCL 21(1) — describes Yimas-Arafundi Pidgin structure; paywalled, not readable online

sources.citation: Foley, William A. 2013. Yimas-Arafundi Pidgin. In Michaelis, Maurer, Haspelmath & Huber (eds.), The Survey of Pidgin and Creole Languages, vol. 3, 105-113. Oxford: OUP; = APiCS Online survey chapter 69 (CC-BY).https://apics-online.info/surveys/69
sources.note: Sec. 4 Phonology gives 4 vowels (/ə/ largely epenthetic, as in Yimas) and 15-16 consonants; zero occurrences of 'stress' or 'accent' in the whole chapter. Only prosodic remark (sec. 8): dependent verbs in clause chains carry a distinctive falling pitch, verbs inside serial verb constructions do not — clause-level intonation, not word stress.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Yimas language' (Yimas-Arafundi_Pidgin redirects there); stress section cites Foley 1991 The Yimas Language of New Guinea, pp. 75-77
sources.note: For the LEXIFIER Yimas proper only (not the pidgin): primary stress on the first syllable, secondary on the third in words of >3 syllables, epenthetic-vowel first syllables skipped (Foley 1991: 75-77). Nothing about stress in the pidgin.
Glottolog's most extensive descriptions: Foley 2013 (grammar sketch, 9 pp.), Foley 2006 (a wordlist or less, 22 pp.), Williams 1993 (a wordlist or less, 2 pp.). No other descriptive references.

sources.citation: APiCS Online structure dataset 69: Yimas-Arafundi Pidgin (Foley).https://apics-online.info/contributions/69
sources.note: Feature-value page (segment inventory); APiCS has no word-stress feature; only source listed besides the chapter is Bakker 2003 on reduplication. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Foley, William A. 1988. Language birth: the processes of pidginization and creolization. In Newmeyer (ed.), Linguistics: The Cambridge Survey IV, 162-183. Cambridge: CUP.

sources.note: Earliest structural sketch of Yimas Pidgin (pp. 168-72, 174-5). Full-text snippet checks (no 'first syllable', 'penultimate', 'prosod*'; 'stressed' only morphosyntactic) suggest it is silent on word stress, but the pages were not read in full. Borrowable scan on archive.org (login required) and paywalled on Cambridge Core.
